items.title: Gauge/diffeomorphism matter identity and field exchange
items.design_state: Complete conditional lemma authored; current M02/M03 suppliers used at inspected draft statements. Seven declared M01 typed replacement item carriers remain absent and their inherited source closure is open; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with metric-selected connection $\nabla$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth principal $U(1)$ bundle with a smooth connection and global curvature two-form $F$, using the local-potential and fixed-sector conventions of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]] and [[lem-emg-circle-connection-gluing]]. Let $\Psi$ be a smooth matter configuration and let $S_m$ be a real differentiable functional of $(g,A,\Psi)$, where $A$ denotes the bundle connection, not necessarily a global one-form.

Fix a configuration at which the matter Euler–Lagrange variation vanishes, meaning $\delta_\Psi S_m=0$ for every smooth compactly supported matter-field variation. Suppose that for all compactly supported metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$ and all compactly supported connection variations $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$ in the fixed bundle sector, the remaining first variation is

$$\delta S_m=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T^m_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+\frac{1}{c}\int_M j^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $c>0$, $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $j$ is a smooth vector field. Assume $S_m$ is invariant under compactly supported gauge transformations and under simultaneous pullback along the local flow of every compactly supported smooth vector field, with the connection and matter field transported by the induced horizontal lift to $P$. Only the local variations at flow parameter $s=0$ are used. Then

$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla_a T_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c,$$

where $j_c:=g_{ca}j^a$. These are conditional variational identities; no Maxwell or Einstein field equation, existence theorem, or empirical premise is assumed.

For SI bookkeeping in length coordinates, take $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-1}}$, and $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$. If $S_m$ is assigned action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$, the displayed variation convention assigns $[T^m]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. These are formal dimensional assignments only; the lemma adopts no matter model or empirical law.
items.strategy: use compact gauge variations to obtain current continuity, then use the horizontal lift of a compactly supported vector field to convert diffeomorphism invariance into the stress-exchange identity.

items.title: Compact Einstein–Hilbert variation and SI coupling
items.design_state: Complete conditional lemma authored; current M02/M03 suppliers used at inspected draft statements. Seven declared M01 typed replacement item carriers remain absent and their inherited source closure is open; readiness escalated. The additional research-only GR-G3 dependency has no production item carrier.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. For a compactly supported metric variation, write $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$, $h_{ab}=\delta g_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$, $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$, and $V^a=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^a{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^d{}_{db}$, where $\delta\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\frac12g^{ad}(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc})$; curvature and Einstein tensors are as in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. The local density identity is

$$\delta((R-2\Lambda)w)=w(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}+\partial_a(wV^a).$$

Fix constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Regard these as formal coefficients; their physical interpretation and units are not assumptions of this mathematical lemma. For smooth metric variations with compact support in the interior, at fixed bundle connection and fixed matter fields, consider the action difference

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}\int_MF_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+S_m,$$

where noncompact action values are used only through compactly supported differences, $F$ is the curvature of a fixed smooth bundle connection, and $S_m$ has Hilbert tensor $T^m$ in the convention of [[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]. Let $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ be the electromagnetic Hilbert tensor supplied by the compact Maxwell variation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]], and set $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. Then for every compactly supported inverse-metric variation $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$,

$$\delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M\left(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})\right)q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently, stationarity under all such metric variations is equivalent to

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}).$$

Any tensor fields satisfying this equation necessarily have $\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})=0$ because $\Lambda$ is constant. This is a compatibility condition, not a claim that the coupled field equations have a solution or that matter and Maxwell equations follow from metric stationarity.

For dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates one may assign $[R]=[\Lambda]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[G_N]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T^m]=[T^{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Then every action term has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$ and $\kappa_E T$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. These are formal assignments only; the lemma assumes no measured parameter value or physical field law.
items.strategy: add the three independent first variations, normalize the common coefficient, and use compactly supported test tensors for the pointwise Euler–Lagrange equation.

items.title: Classical complex-scalar connection derivative and action
items.design_state: Complete conditional definition authored; current M02/M03 suppliers used at inspected draft statements. Seven declared M01 typed replacement item carriers remain absent and their inherited source closure is open; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Set $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with multiplication. Let $P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle in the sense of [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]], with a fixed smooth connection. Choose local trivializations and normalized real connection potentials $A_i$ as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. On any overlap neighborhood admitting a smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$, write $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$. Use the dual representation $\rho_k(z):=z^{-k}$ and define charged scalar representatives by the global transition rule $\varphi_j=g_{ij}^{k}\varphi_i$, equivalently $e^{ikf_{ij}}\varphi_i$ on each phase-lift neighborhood; the connection rule there is

$$A_j=A_i+\kappa_0\,df_{ij}.$$

Here $\kappa_0>0$ is the chosen circle normalization with $[\kappa_0]=\mathrm{Wb}$, $k\in\mathbb Z$ is the representation weight, and $\lambda:=k/\kappa_0$ has units $\mathrm{Wb}^{-1}$. Because $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ and $k$ is an integer, the maps $g_{ij}^{k}$ satisfy the scalar transition cocycle. A charged scalar is a family of smooth local functions $\varphi_i$ satisfying this rule; all phase-lift calculations below are local, and no global phase lift is assumed. The constant $c>0$ is the length-to-time conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with units $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Define $F|_{U_i}:=dA_i$; the transition law gives $dA_j=dA_i$, so $F$ is a global curvature two-form. In a global real-potential model on a trivial bundle, one may instead take a global $A$ and any real $\lambda$; no charge quantization is imposed there.

In a local trivialization define the gauge-covariant derivative and its lower-index one-form by

$$P_a:=(D\varphi)_a:=\partial_a\varphi_i-i\lambda A_{i,a}\varphi_i.$$

The transition laws give $P_{j,a}=e^{ikf_{ij}}P_{i,a}$, since $\lambda\kappa_0=k$. For any charged covector $Q_b$ with the same phase transition, define the gauge- and metric-covariant derivative by $D_aQ_b:=\nabla_aQ_b-i\lambda A_aQ_b$ in a local trivialization; for a charged scalar $\eta$, set $D_a\eta:=\partial_a\eta-i\lambda A_a\eta$. Conjugate fields use the opposite gauge sign. Thus $D_aP_b$ is a well-defined charged covariant two-tensor, and $D_aP^a:=g^{ab}D_aP_b$. Consequently $|\varphi|^2$ and $g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$ are global scalar fields. Let $V:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth on an open set $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the range of $|\varphi|^2$, write $V'$ for its ordinary real derivative, and choose a positive normalization constant $K_\varphi>0$.

The kinetic scalar $g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$ is real because its complex conjugate equals itself by symmetry of $g^{ab}$. Put

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad S_\varphi:=-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}\int_M L_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

For SI dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates, take $[\varphi]=1$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[P_a]=\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[V]=\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $[K_\varphi]=\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-1}$; then $S_\varphi$ has units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$. These are formal dimensional assignments, not measured values or physical postulates. On noncompact $M$, the integral is used when finite; otherwise only differences between configurations agreeing outside a compact set are defined, so every variation below is a compactly supported integral.

Allowed first variations are compactly supported smooth complex-section variations $\delta\varphi$, compactly supported real global one-form variations $\alpha=\delta A$ added to every local $A_i$ (so the same bundle transition functions are retained), and compactly supported symmetric inverse-metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$. The formula defines a classical mathematical functional; it asserts no quantum interpretation, value of $\hbar$, or material-response model.
items.strategy: verify that the scalar transition maps form a line bundle, that the covariant derivative and action density patch globally, and that the stated dimensions agree.

items.title: Classical charged-scalar action, current and stress variation
items.design_state: Complete conditional lemma authored; current M02/M03 suppliers used at inspected draft statements. Seven declared M01 typed replacement item carriers remain absent and their inherited source closure is open; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
Use the scalar functional of [[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]] on a fixed smooth bundle sector, with $K_\varphi>0$, real $\lambda$, real smooth $V$, and smooth $\varphi,A,g$. Write $P_a:=D_a\varphi$ and define the gauge- and metric-covariant derivative of its one-form by

$$D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b,$$

with the conjugate derivative using $+i\lambda A_a$. For compactly supported variations, define

$$E_\varphi:=D_aP^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\,\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi.$$

Then the scalar-field variation is $\delta_\varphi S_\varphi=\frac{K_\varphi}{c}\operatorname{Re}\int_M\overline{\delta\varphi}\,E_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g$; stationarity in every compactly supported complex scalar direction is equivalent to $E_\varphi=0$. The connection and inverse-metric variations are

$$\delta_A S_\varphi=\frac1c\int_Mj^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,\qquad \delta_gS_\varphi=-\frac1{2c}\int_MT^\varphi_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

The following off-shell identities also hold:

$$\nabla_a j^a=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi E_\varphi),\qquad \nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_\varphi}P_b)+F_{ba}j^a.$$

In particular, the matter equation $E_\varphi=0$ implies current conservation and the exact Lorentz-force exchange identity $\nabla_a(T^\varphi)^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c$. No coupled Einstein–Maxwell solution or empirical matter model is asserted.

Under the formal SI assignments of [[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]], $j^a$ has units $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ and $T^\varphi$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$; this dimensional check is not an empirical claim.
items.strategy: compute the three compact first variations, then differentiate the current and stress expressions using the gauge-covariant product rule.

items.title: Curved electromagnetic stress divergence
items.design_state: Complete conditional lemma authored; current M02/M03 suppliers used at inspected draft statements. Seven declared M01 typed replacement item carriers remain absent and their inherited source closure is open; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
Let $U$ be an oriented open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(U)$ and $j\in\Gamma(TU)$ be smooth, and let $\mu_0>0$. Assume

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

with the sign convention of [[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. Define the Maxwell Hilbert tensor by the compact metric variation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]],

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

Then

$$\nabla_aT_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}=-F^{bc}j_c.$$

All fields and derivatives are smooth on $U$. In length-coordinate SI bookkeeping, assign $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$; these are formal units and not observed values. No quadratic stress is assigned to singular point self-fields or distributional sources.
items.strategy: differentiate the variational Maxwell tensor, contract the homogeneous Maxwell identity with $F$, and cancel the derivative terms.

items.title: Exact background scalar plane wave and derived current
items.design_state: Complete conditional example authored; current M02/M03 suppliers used at inspected draft statements. Seven declared M01 typed replacement item carriers remain absent and their inherited source closure is open; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
On $\mathbb R^4$ with $x^0=ct$, Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and trivial bundle, set $A=0$, $V(u)=m_s^2u$ with $m_s>0$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and

$$\varphi(t,\mathbf x)=C\exp(-i\omega t+i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x),$$

where $C\ne0$ is dimensionless, $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$ has units $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and $\omega:=c\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+m_s^2}>0$ has units $\mathrm s^{-1}$. For the scalar action of [[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]], this is an exact solution of the local background scalar equation, equivalently stationary under compactly supported scalar variations. The infinite-volume action value need not be finite; only the local equation and compactly supported variations are used. If the coupling $\lambda\ne0$, the same configuration has a nonzero derived current although $F=dA=0$, so it fails the sourced Maxwell equation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. It is therefore a background scalar solution, not a solution of the coupled scalar–Maxwell system. No relation to $\hbar$ or empirical data is used.
